To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spectral methods, especially the Burg algorithm, are very useful in monitoring the mechanical parts of rotating machines, in particular the bearing defects.
The application of spectral analysis methods to rotating machinery is a promising approach to the development of condition-based maintenance for industrial machinery.

(1) AR spectral analysis can be applied to detect and track the degradation of the mechanical components of rotating machinery; (2) AR spectral analysis is a promising tool for condition-based maintenance; (3) AR spectral analysis has a high-resolution power and can detect defects in the bearings of the rotating machines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method of condition monitoring for rotating machinery.
the application of parametric spectral analysis methods in the field of mechanical component monitoring.
the use of spectral analysis techniques for the detection of mechanical components faults in a turning machine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the parametric spectral analysis methods have been successfully applied to the monitoring of the mechanical components of rotating machine, and that they are very powerful tools to be used in a predictive maintenance program.
the parametric spectral analysis methods have a better performance in the fault detection than the non-parametric methods.
the parametric methods are more efficient in detecting and tracking faults than the classical methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the parametric spectral analysis techniques, based on the modelization of the signal by the calculation of the spectral estimates, have been tested and compared with the classical spectral analysis methods.
we have been successful in demonstrating that the parametric methods can provide the same results as the classical methods in the case of the bearing faults.
the parametric methods of analysis are more efficient in the detection of defects in bearings and gears than the classical methods of analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

parametric methods are more powerful than classical nonparametric methods for fault detection in rotating machinery, and that the parametric methods we used are able to detect faults in the bearing system of the machine.
, for the case of the bearing defect, the use of parametric methods is not necessary.
the AR spectral analysis methods provide a better resolution in the frequency domain than the classical spectral analysis methods (such as the correlogram).
